answer: Operator-Linked Reputation Decay. Each agent identity carries a reputation kernel tied to a verified operator record, not the wallet. When a cluster is flagged as sybil, the protocol applies a ripple penalty: the operator's reputation score decays across every identity under that record, throttling new registrations and cutting fee rebates. A single flagged plume of sock-puppets therefore drags the operator's whole fleet. Attacker cost is loss of throughput and rebates on all linked identities, forcing fresh operator onboarding per attempt.
